tagline.text: Water sports and lakeside leisure on a reservoir in the Sierra Madre foothills

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱1,500–5,000 (transport, meals and activities; accommodation extra for an overnight stay; rough estimate)

children.text: Lake Caliraya is a roughly 1,050-hectare reservoir spanning Lumban, Cavinti and Kalayaan in Laguna. It is a leisure destination near Manila where you can wakeboard, windsurf and fish for bass, then relax at a lakeside resort.

Lake Caliraya is an artificial lake spanning the municipalities of Lumban, Cavinti and Kalayaan in Laguna. According to Wikipedia, it has a surface area of about 1,050 hectares, a maximum length of about 8 km and a maximum width of about 3 km, and more than 30 islands, many of them unnamed. The largest is said to be about the size of Rizal Park. It lies in the highlands of the Sierra Madre foothills, about 100 km east of Manila. Elevation figures differ between sources. Wikipedia notes that the lake floor is very soft clay.

The lake was created with the construction of the Caliraya Dam. According to Wikipedia, work on the dam began in 1939 under Lt. Col. Hugh J. Casey of the US Army Corps of Engineers with the approval of President Manuel L. Quezon, as a project to supply hydroelectric power to Southern Luzon. The dam was sabotaged by retreating American forces in 1942 and by Japanese forces in 1944, rebuilt after the war and inaugurated in 1953 by the National Power Corporation (NAPOCOR). The hydroelectric plant was refurbished in 2004. The lake is still known as part of the Kalayaan pumped-storage power system together with nearby Lumot Lake.

In the late 1960s the Nieto and De Padua families "rediscovered" the area and promoted it to Manila's elite and expatriate community, and the Sierra Lakes subdivision and the Dos Lagos Club (now Lagos del Sol) were developed. A Japanese government grant helped pave the main access road, and by the mid-1980s golf clubs and resorts such as Caliraya Springs had been built. As a result, the shores today mix vacation homes, upscale houses and resorts, and Wikipedia says it ranks as the most popular bass fishing spot in the Philippines.

Things to do include wakeboarding, windsurfing, kiteboarding, jet skiing, water skiing, boating, bass fishing, golf and camping. One travel guide says the afternoon winds are reliable, which is good for windsurfing and sailing, and describes December–May as the dry season (about
) and June–November as the wet season (about
). Opening hours and prices vary greatly by resort, so check the latest information.

Caliraya is known for resorts with wakeboarding, sport fishing and water-sport operators. Wikipedia lists windsurfing, kiteboarding, jet skiing and water skiing among the pastimes. Prices differ by operator and season, so check when you book.
Since early developers stocked it with bass, the lake has ranked as the most popular bass fishing spot in the Philippines. Ask your resort or locals about fishing rules and boat rental.

On the Cavinti and Lumban shores there are places to stay such as Caliraya EcoVille Farm Resort, Kaliraya Surf Kamp and Sofia's Lake Resort (on Lumot Lake). Guides from 2020 to 2022 listed a lakeside cottage at about ₱2,500–3,500 (for 2 people) and tent camping at about ₱500 per person, so check recent prices.

blocks.title: Lake loops by bike or motorbike

children.text: It is a popular weekend route for riders from eastern Manila. One cycling guide describes a loop of about
35 km
from Caliraya via Lumot Lake to Cavinti and Pagsanjan. Mobile signal is weak and map apps sometimes route you on roads that are blocked, so prepare an offline map.

One guide named Yhamshe Grill, Meldivz Mountain View and Alexa's at Caliraya Heights as restaurants with views of the lake and ridges. Trattoria Altrove at Kaliraya Surf Kamp was also recommended. Check whether they are open before you go.

Wikipedia describes Lumot Lake as an auxiliary reservoir for Caliraya and less developed. There are also places to stay on islands, such as Sofia's Lake Resort, which suit a quiet overnight stay. You get around on the lake by boat.

The Cavinti underground river and cave complex requires advance reservations and a permit, and a 2013 guide said visitors were limited and an environmental fee of about ₱10 was charged. Ask the Cavinti tourism office for the latest rules.

Cavinti Falls, close to the lake (another name for Pagsanjan Falls on the Cavinti side), can be reached by trek and by boat, and the Pagsanjan gorge boat tour is popular in its own right. Adding a waterfall to a lake day is possible, but travel time grows, so it is easier to choose just one than to fit everything in. Ask the Cavinti tourism office about access to the falls on the Cavinti side and the fees.

Arrive at a lakeside resort, check whether day use is available and the fee, and enjoy wakeboarding or kayaking.
Have lunch at a restaurant with a view.
Take a slow drive around the lake and take photos at viewpoints.
Watch the sunset and head home. If you are uneasy about driving mountain roads at night, leave early.
Some resorts may not accept day visitors, so be sure to check before booking.

From Lumban choose the right fork toward Lake Caliraya. Parking differs by resort.
The road winds in the mountains, so take care when driving at night.

items.title: By bus and jeepney from Manila

children.text: Take HM Transport or DLTB from Cubao, or Green Star or DLTB from Pasay, to Santa Cruz. A 2013 guide gave the fare as
, and a more recent guide put Manila–Santa Cruz buses at about ₱180–300 (confirm locally).
In Santa Cruz take a jeepney to Cavinti for about
(2013), then a Lumban–Cavinti jeepney to the lake. Inside the lake area you may need a tricycle or a resort pickup.
Public transport involves many transfers and takes half a day or more, so leave early.

There is also a route from Ortigas along the Manila East Road through Antipolo, Tanay, Pililla, Siniloan, Pakil, Paete and Lumban, then up to the lake. One cycling guide says it is over 100 km from Quezon City with about 1,100 m of total elevation gain.
For motorbike riders and cycling fans, the route beside the lake is appealing.
December–May is relatively cool and dry and the best time for lake activities. One guide rates February–April as "Excellent." The afternoon wind is steady, which suits windsurfing and sailing.

June–November is the rainy season with afternoon showers, and October is described as the wettest month. If the weather is bad, lake activities can be cancelled, so check the refund policy when you book.

There are many resorts and villa-style accommodations along the shore. One guide listed rates at Caliraya EcoVille Farm Resort of ₱2,500 for a hut, ₱2,999 for a premium lakeside cottage or air-conditioned room, and ₱500 per person for a tent (2020–2022 guides). Sofia's Lake Resort on Lumot Lake had its soft opening in May 2023 and was listed with guesthouse rates of ₱3,300 per person, among others. Prices at specific places change often, so check before booking.

For meals, view restaurants (Yhamshe Grill, Meldivz Mountain View and Alexa's at Caliraya Heights) and Trattoria Altrove at Kaliraya Surf Kamp were mentioned, and one account remembers a bowl of lugaw (rice porridge) by the lake. For groceries, Lumban or Cavinti town is the easiest.
Check before you book whether day use is allowed. Not every resort accepts day visitors.
Mobile signal is weak, so download offline maps.
For windsurfing and sailing, the wind is stronger in the late afternoon. Rather than piloting an unfamiliar boat yourself, hire a local one. Guides say there are hidden shoals in shallow areas.
If you are cycling the loop, leave extra time in case you have to turn back at blocked roads.
The Cavinti caves need a permit in advance. Contact the Cavinti tourism office at 523-0152.
Bring a rain jacket and a waterproof bag. The weather in the mountains can change quickly.
The Japanese Garden was reported closed to the public as of May 2022, so check before you visit.
With so much water-sports activity, the lake has many boats and jet skis. When swimming, wear a life jacket and keep out of boating areas.
Do not pilot an unfamiliar boat on the lake yourself. Guides mention shallow shoals and obstacles.
On the road toward the caves there are no-trespassing signs and blocked paths. Do not trust the route your map app suggests.
The road down to the Cavinti caves is very steep and hard on brakes.
Wikipedia notes that New People's Army (NPA) members were present in the area in the 1980s, but check the current situation locally.
Prices and opening hours vary by operator, so check the latest notices.
